summary: WebSocket multiplexing + upstream migration produces stale-ack partial delta and missing trailing tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports repeated partial streaming outputs when their client performs websocket multiplexing and a connection migration (upstream proxy/ALB rebind). Instead of receiving the final delta tokens, the client sees a short ‘stale-ack’ fragment and the stream stops without the usual closing metadata.

Impact:
- Several user-facing generation requests for BrightCart chat flows are missing the final sentence(s) ~10-15% of the time during bursts.
- Affected feature: live product-recommendation snippets in the BrightCart web checkout (high commercial impact).
- Occurs only on their Dedicated tenancy during peak traffic and after upstream path changes (ALB handoff / proxy connection reuse).

Observed behavior:
- Client receives a short delta (usually 1-4 tokens) identified as a stale-ack, then the websocket stream emits a normal keepalive, but the final closing metadata ("event: end"/json envelope) is not observed by the client.
- When the client reconnects and re-requests the session, the server returns the expected final content (so not a model generation fault), indicating partial delivery rather than model truncation.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Use BrightCart SDK with multiplexing enabled (multiple concurrent streams on same ws connection).
2) Start 20 concurrent generation requests targeting redwood/gptx-1.2b with short prompts (~80 tokens target).
3) Simulate upstream ALB rebind by toggling a TCP drain on a path (they used an internal test harness to induce connection migration).
4) Observe ~10-15% of streams deliver a short stale fragment and then never observe terminal envelope.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming session should deliver full deltas followed by closing metadata (end-of-stream marker). Reconnect/resume logic should not lose trailing tokens.

Temporary workaround provided by customer:
- Disable client-side multiplexing (use single-stream-per-connection) which reduces incidence to <1%.
- Implement server-side poll-on-reconnect for missing terminal metadata (application-layer workaround).

Logs / sample traces (sanitized):
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z ws-client[bc-123] -> SEND: start_stream id=stream-91
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> UPSTREAM: attach worker-17
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z serving-runtime[worker-17] -> GENERATION: stream-91 partial=..."The recommended item is a RedWidget..."
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> CLIENT: delta tokens: 1-4, flagged as stale-ack
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> CLIENT: keepalive
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> UPSTREAM: connection handoff (ALB rebind)
- 2026-03-09T18:02:14Z ws-client[bc-123] -> RECONNECT: start_stream id=stream-91
- 2026-03-09T18:02:14Z serving-runtime[worker-18] -> GENERATION: stream-91 final payload sent on reconnect

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Multiplexing conflates per-stream ack windows in the websocket-proxy during an upstream connection migration. A stale-ack tag is emitted when the proxy believes a downstream socket has acknowledged the tail, but the original upstream still had outstanding buffered payloads.
- Hypothesis 2: The serving-runtime sends closing metadata but the proxy's per-stream frame mapping loses the final envelope when multiple streams share a single underlying TCP connection and a path change occurs.
- We reproduced a lower-frequency case internally by running a multiplexed client against a test ALB and forcing connection drain; captured pcap shows final TCP segments being retransmitted but client-side frame reassembly stops at keepalive.

Next steps (assigned):
- Network/edge to add per-stream frame counters and assert end-envelope delivery across migration boundaries (Liam Chen).
- Runtime to add end-of-stream explicit flush on detection of upstream handoff (SRE pair: Olga Novak + runtime team).
- SDK/Client team to ship a temporary patch to disable multiplexing by default for Dedicated customers until a fix is in place (PR opened).

Attachments:
- pcap snippet: https://s3.redwood.com/brightcart/pcap/1003456.pcap (customer-provided)
- Internal trace: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streams/trace/stream-91

investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally at low frequency by enabling multiplexing in our internal sdk and toggling connection drain on ALB.
- Packet capture shows server final frames transmitted but not reassembled client-side; proxy logs show stale_ack flag set immediately before rebind.
- Reviewed ws-proxy code path: per-stream window bookkeeping relies on a single seq counter that gets reset on connection rebind. Probable race between rebind cleanup and in-flight frame drain.
- Quick patch idea: persist per-stream sequence state across rebinds for N seconds and hold rebind completion until outstanding frames are acked or TTL expires.
resolution: In progress: workaround (disable multiplexing) accepted by customer. Engineering to implement proxy-side per-stream sequence preservation and explicit end-of-stream flush on handoff. Estimated fix ETA: 2 sprints (priority patch + canary).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and pcap. I can confirm patterns look like a delivery gap rather than model truncation. Starting triage with edge team.

2026-03-11 - Olga Novak (SRE): Able to reproduce at ~4% locally with a stress harness. Captured pcaps show server final frames transmitted but client reassembly drops them when multiplexed. Opening INT ticket for proxy seq state investigation.
2026-03-11 - BrightCart (customer): Disabling multiplexing reduced errors to near-zero. We can keep multiplexing off short-term but need a fix since multiplexing is critical for our scaling model.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen (Edge Eng): Implemented a debug build that persists per-stream counters across rebind; can reproduce the stale-ack race. Proposing a gating flush on handoff and a short buffer window. Will open PR and coordinate canary with BrightCart.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel (Support): SLA ticket updated; will notify customer once canary passes. Follow-up: coordinate with BrightCart to schedule low-traffic canary slot.
